_about: REAL curated splits grounded in FWA data + the fishing synopsis. One worked example per anchor kind, all verified against data/bc_fisheries_data.gpkg. Every split defines a CUT that slices the targeted channel(s). `_comment`/`_about` are ignored by from_dict; `_concern` is a real (optional) field surfaced in splits.resolved.json + the gpkg. See splits.schema.md and docs/04.

splits._comment: LAKE — 'Adams River (upstream/downstream of Adams Lake)'. Adams Lake wbk=329014384 IS the Adams River blk 356362743. The lake already splits the BLK in the graph build, so this is a no-op split kept for matching (the boundary + label already exist).
splits.label: Adams Lake

splits._comment: POINT — 'Kootenay River (downstream of the Idaho border)'. The Kootenay (blk 356570348) crosses the 49th parallel TWICE; this coord is the Creston-area crossing (verified m~=168733). With border auto-splits on, this point falls within proximity of the border split and PICKS IT UP (no second cut) — the label just names that boundary the way the reg does.
splits.label: Idaho border

splits._comment: LAKE — 'Kootenay River (upstream of Koocanusa Reservoir)'. Lake Koocanusa IS in FWA as manmade waterbody wbk 328961702 (verified: a lake node threading the Kootenay). Like Adams this is a no-op split that relabels the boundary the lake already made — the reservoir head sits ~47m above the Kootenay's BC border re-entry (which is why an earlier point+border-pickup produced a sliver; the lake anchor is exact).
splits.label: Koocanusa Reservoir

splits._comment: POINT (obstacle) — 'Hunlen Creek (upstream of Hunlen Falls)'. Hunlen Falls (gazetted lon/lat) snaps onto Hunlen Creek (blk 360862431) at m~=1685, 15.6m off — the ~260m falls plunging into the Atnarko valley near the mouth. Upstream reach (1685->32698) is the excepted water. Coord source: FISS obstacle / gazetteer; the obstacles layer (WHSE_FISH.FISS_OBSTACLES_PNT_SP) can supply this automatically in future.
splits.label: Hunlen Falls

splits._comment: POINT — 'Young Creek (upstream of Hwy 20)'. Hwy 20 crossing (lon/lat) snaps onto Young Creek (blk 360862631) at 2.6m. Upstream reach is the excepted water.
splits.label: Hwy 20

splits._comment: CONFLUENCE (WSC-keyed) — 'Burnt Bridge Creek (upstream of Sitkatapa Creek)'. Burnt Bridge (blk 360883785, WSC ...777225) is split where its DIRECT tributary (WSC ...777225-504013 = blk 360844922) joins. Verified: that tributary's WSC = parent WSC + one level (a self-validating confluence). The creek is UNNAMED in FWA; 'Sitkatapa Creek' is inferred from Sitkatapa Lake sitting up its second fork (WSC ...504013-327666 = blk 360855126) — see _concern + the name_variant entry.
splits.label: Sitkatapa Creek
splits._concern: Tributary name 'Sitkatapa Creek' is INFERRED (FWA-unnamed); named for Sitkatapa Lake up its upper fork (blk 360855126). No alternative name available. Added as a name_variant with the same note.

splits._comment: MU BOUNDARY — 'Fraser River' region-2 / region-3 boundary (blk 356364114). VERIFIED: 2-17/3-15 are NOT adjacent (the previously authored pair was wrong). The adjacent region-2/3 pair on the Fraser is 2-18 / 3-14, whose shared boundary crosses the Fraser at EXACTLY ONE point (m~=196967, near Hope). The resolver collapses to a single split; a multi-crossing boundary would be deduped + flagged (_concern).
splits.label: Region 2 / Region 3

splits._comment: POINT — 'Coquihalla River (Othello Tunnels — upper/N tunnel entrance)'. Othello Tunnels upper-most railway tunnel, N entrance (page-24 reg map). Pairs with coquihalla_othello_lower_tunnel to bound the ~700 m tunnel-interior closure reach; the entry's rules attach upstream-of / at / downstream-of these two landmarks. Targets Coquihalla River by gnis_id 19983 (_target_blks resolves gnis_id -> its blk[s]).
splits.label: the upper Othello railway tunnel (N entrance)

splits._comment: POINT — 'Coquihalla River (Othello Tunnels — lower/S tunnel entrance)'. Othello Tunnels lower-most railway tunnel, S entrance (page-24 reg map). Pairs with coquihalla_othello_upper_tunnel to bound the ~700 m Othello Tunnels closure reach.
splits.label: the lower Othello railway tunnel (S entrance)

splits._comment: POINT — Wigwam River km-42 divide. TWO regs bound this ONE point from opposite sides: 'WIGWAM RIVER CW (downstream of the access road adjacent to km 42 on the Bighorn (Ram) FSR)' and 'WIGWAM RIVER CW (upstream of the Forest Service recreation site adjacent to km 42 ...)'. The access road and the FS rec site are adjacent (same location at the km-42 marker / junction of the Wigwam River FSR and the Ram Creek FSR), so a single cut yields the downstream reach + the upstream reach and both rules attach (one downstream_of, one upstream_of). Targets Wigwam River by gnis_id 2311 (_target_blks resolves gnis_id -> its blk[s]); MU 4-2, Region 4 Kootenay. Coord = FS rec site (Lat 49.18220 N, Lon 114.95794 W). Corroborated by overrides note: 'Divide is approximately at Linear Feature ID 706869683'.
splits.label: km 42 on the Bighorn (Ram) Forest Service Road
splits._concern: NOT yet built/verified — run build.py on the Wigwam extent and confirm the point snaps onto blk(s) for gnis 2311 within proximity and yields a downstream/upstream pair. The two regs phrase the landmark differently ('access road' vs 'Forest Service recreation site') though they mark the same km-42 point; Phase-5 location_identifier narrowing must map both wordings to this one split label.

splits._comment: POINT (obstacle) — Whiteswan Lake OUTLET-STREAM falls. Reg entry 'WHITESWAN LAKE'S INLET & OUTLET STREAMS' (Region 4, MU 4-24) is closure EXCEPT 'the outlet stream downstream of the falls 2.4 km downstream of Whiteswan Lake', and that excepted reach then carries its own rules (No Fishing Aug 1-Mar 31; rainbow quota=5 C&R others when open). This split cuts the outlet stream at that falls so the downstream reach becomes its own section. Falls = FISS obstacle point id 21225 ('Falls', WSC-50K 349-666200-32000) at Lat 50.17300 N, Lon 115.46190 W. Verified against FWA: the falls sits 6.7 m off blue line 356560775 (FWA_WATERSHED_CODE 300-625474-814939-312002 = the same 50K code 349-666200-32000; GNIS null = UNNAMED, which is why the reg entry is not_found). Targets that blk directly (gnis is null; the obstacle's 50K WSC won't match the streams' 20K code, so blk is the safe key).
splits.label: the falls 2.4 km downstream of Whiteswan Lake
splits._concern: NOT yet built/verified — run build.py on the Whiteswan extent and confirm the point snaps onto blk 356560775 (~6.7 m off) and yields a downstream reach. Separately, resolving the base entry 'WHITESWAN LAKE'S INLET & OUTLET STREAMS' needs a NEW lake-immediate-IO operator (lake_inlets ∪ lake_outlets), NOT the full tributary closure — see review notes; the tier0 parse flags includes_tributaries/tributary_only which conflicts with the 'immediate inlets/outlets only' reading and belongs in the corrections memo.

splits._comment: AREA_BOUNDARY (tributary-scoped) — cut the Pitt River (gnis 7551, WSC 100-025956) AND every one of its WSC descendants where they cross the Garibaldi Park polygon boundary; the build then flags every resulting piece whose midpoint is INSIDE the polygon with in_areas=['Garibaldi Park'] -> location_identifier 'within Garibaldi Park'. RULE-AGNOSTIC: this only establishes the geometric fact of park membership + the boundary cuts; Phase-5 matching later attaches the 'No Fishing within Garibaldi Park' closure to the in_areas pieces. WSC-descendant scope (not gnis, which is mainstem-only) catches blk 356350872, which leaves the park then re-enters — a point split cannot. Measured (docs/15 §10): 20 blks cross the boundary (21 crossings, 1 re-enter); mainstem 27 km inside. Garibaldi is a PROVINCIAL park (code PP) closed only by this named reg (a curated closure, exempt from the 'never render closed for provincial parks' flag).
splits.label: Garibaldi Park
splits._concern: NOT yet built/verified — run build.py --gnis 'Pitt River' --splits with parks_bc loaded; confirm ~20 boundary crossings, the mainstem split once into a ~27 km 'within Garibaldi Park' piece, and blk 356350872's middle segment flagged inside. Human-verify a crossing near 49.73752,-122.75042. parks_bc must be a fetched/loaded layer in the build's gpkg.

splits._comment: CONFLUENCE (WSC-keyed) — 'Chemainus River (downstream/upstream of Bannon Creek)' (Region 1, MU 1-5). ONE confluence cut at the mouth of Bannon Creek (FWA gazettes it 'Banon Creek', single N; tributary blk 354135507, WSC 920-302830-171638, a direct child of Chemainus River WSC 920-302830) yields BOTH the downstream-of and upstream-of reaches; the reg's two rules (No Fishing downstream Jul 1-Sep 30 / upstream Dec 1-Sep 30) attach one to each side. Locators chemainus-river-79cc9a (downstream) + -688d54 (upstream) both map here — SHARED split. The third Chemainus locator (Copper Canyon Falls) is a separate point split, already curated (chemainus-river-07756e). Mouth coord [-123.75806,48.90332] validated parent-at-mouth = Chemainus River at 0.0 m; ~1.7 km NE of the Copper Canyon Falls point (consistent).
splits.label: Bannon Creek
splits._concern: NOT yet built/verified — run build.py on the Chemainus extent and confirm the confluence (tributary_wsc 920-302830-171638 = blk 354135507) cuts Chemainus blk 354154440 into a downstream/upstream pair. FWA name is 'Banon Creek' (one N) — a name_variant may be wanted so the reg's 'Bannon Creek' matches.

splits._comment: POINT — 'John Hart Lake's Tributaries — No Fishing Apr 15-Jul 15 (includes channel downstream of Ladore Dam)' (Region 1, MU 1-10). Point split at the Ladore Dam face on the Campbell River mainstem (blk 354154635, WSC 920-627155). Ladore Dam is the BC Hydro dam between Strathcona Dam and John Hart Dam; the reg's 'channel downstream of Ladore Dam' is the reach running from the dam toward John Hart Lake, so the dam is its head / split point. Coord [-125.38949,50.01217] = Lower Campbell Lake outlet (the dam) snapped to the mainstem; web-sourced (mapcarta 'Ladore Dam and Generating Station' 50.01209,-125.38962) then FWA-validated (4.3 m off the reservoir edge, 12.9 m off the mainstem). Human-confirmed dam-face (not the John Hart Lake inlet ~1.9 km downstream). Locator john-hart-lake-s-tributaries-36c501 maps here.
splits.label: Ladore Dam
splits._concern: NOT yet built/verified — run build.py on the Campbell extent and confirm the point snaps onto blk 354154635 within proximity and yields a downstream reach. Coord is web-sourced + snapped (no FWA dam feature in this gpkg); confirm on satellite at 50.0121,-125.3896.
